client.label: Retail Banking SPA
client.overview: Serves as the unified presentation layer and digital front-door for the retail banking platform, delivering specialized, role-tailored web interfaces for Retail Customers, Branch Tellers (Ledger Reviewers), and Platform Compliance Administrators. Built on React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, the single-page application enforces strict client-side validation against JSR-380 constraints (such as 4-decimal currency input masking for Philippine Peso amounts), manages short-lived JWT access tokens strictly in volatile memory via React AuthContext, and transparently negotiates silent token refresh cycles using HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies to guard against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) token exfiltration. For branch tellers, it provides an interactive Maker-Checker review console that streams pending high-value transactions (> 10,000,000.0000 PHP) with balance hold indicators and enforces strict segregation of duties by blocking self-approval. The client communicates exclusively with the Spring Cloud API Gateway over TLS 1.3, translating network faults into standardized RFC-7807 problem detail toasts.

specs.runtime: React 19.0.0, TypeScript 5.4, Vite 5.2, Tailwind CSS 3.4 (Served via Nginx 1.25 Alpine)
specs.protocol: HTTPS / TLS 1.3, WebSocket (WSS for real-time notification toasts)
specs.concurrency_model: Single-threaded JavaScript event loop with React 19 Concurrent Mode, Suspense boundaries, and non-blocking Axios promise pipelines
specs.persistence_tier: Volatile in-memory React Context (AuthContext) and TanStack Query cache; HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies for refresh tokens (no raw JWTs or secrets stored in LocalStorage or SessionStorage)
specs.sla_target: Initial DOM Content Loaded < 800ms, client-side route transitions < 100ms, form input validation & masking < 16ms (60fps)

core_mechanisms.name: Volatile In-Memory Token Management & Axios Interceptor Pipeline
core_mechanisms.description: Stores the 15-minute Bearer JWT in volatile React Context memory rather than browser LocalStorage or SessionStorage to prevent XSS-based credential theft. An Axios request interceptor attaches the Authorization header to every outgoing API call.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Axios interceptor intercepts outgoing requests, attaching 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'; on HTTP 401 response, it queues concurrent requests and invokes the silent refresh pipeline before retrying.

core_mechanisms.name: Strict 4-Decimal Currency Masking & Perimeter JSR-380 Client Validation
core_mechanisms.description: Enforces financial number precision rules directly at the user interface boundary, restricting input to numeric characters with exactly up to four decimal places and positive non-zero values before allowing form dispatch.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Custom CurrencyInput component backed by Regex `^\d{1,14}(\.\d{1,4})?$` ensuring alignment with backend `@Digits(integer=14, fraction=4)` and `@Positive` constraints.

core_mechanisms.name: Maker-Checker Segregated Dashboard & Dual-Control Enforcement
core_mechanisms.description: Provides dedicated views for Ledger Reviewers to inspect high-value transfer requests held in PENDING_APPROVAL. Disables the approval action if the authenticated teller's user_id matches the transfer maker_user_id.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: PendingReviewQueue component checks `currentUser.id !== transfer.maker_user_id`; disables action button and renders 'Self-Approval Forbidden (Segregation of Duties)' badge.

core_mechanisms.name: Transparent Silent Token Refresh via HttpOnly Cookie Interception
core_mechanisms.description: Maintains persistent user sessions securely through Refresh Token Rotation (RTR). When the short-lived access token expires, the client sends an empty POST to `/api/v1/auth/refresh`, allowing the browser to automatically submit the secure cookie.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Endpoint `/api/v1/auth/refresh` called with `withCredentials: true`; receives rotated access token in JSON body and new rotated cookie in Set-Cookie header.

core_mechanisms.name: Optimistic UI Isolation with Rollback on RFC-7807 Problem Details
core_mechanisms.description: Displays immediate visual feedback upon action dispatch while tracking asynchronous outbox polling status. If a backend validation or balance check fails, the UI rolls back optimistic state and renders RFC-7807 field error mappings.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: React Query `useMutation` with `onMutate` rollback snapshot and `onError` handler parsing `invalid_params` array into form field error annotations.

gateway.label: API Gateway
gateway.overview: Acts as the reverse-proxy perimeter guardian and single ingress entry point for all incoming HTTP traffic into the containerized banking network. Engineered on Spring Cloud Gateway and Spring Security 6 using the reactive, non-blocking Project Reactor and Netty framework, the gateway enforces cryptographically verified JWT bearer tokens, checks token revocation status against Redis in under 5 milliseconds, applies distributed token-bucket rate limiting per IP and authenticated user, and terminates unauthorized traffic before it can touch internal microservices. It transparently decorates downstream headers with sanitized user claims (X-User-Id, X-User-Role, X-Client-IP), normalizes cross-cutting CORS policies, and formats all perimeter rejections into standardized RFC-7807 Problem Details.

specs.runtime: Spring Cloud Gateway 2023.0.x on Spring Boot 3.3.x, OpenJDK 21 LTS, Netty Reactive Engine
specs.protocol: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TLS 1.3 ingress; HTTP/1.1 JSON downstream
specs.concurrency_model: Non-blocking event loop powered by Netty event loops (Reactor Netty) with minimal OS thread overhead
specs.persistence_tier: Stateless; communicates over RESP to Redis cache (:6379) for token revocation sets and distributed rate limiter buckets
specs.sla_target: Perimeter validation overhead < 5ms at 99.9th percentile under 2,000 concurrent connections

core_mechanisms.name: Stateless HMAC-SHA256 JWT Verification & Claims Extraction
core_mechanisms.description: Validates the cryptographic signature of the Bearer access token on every incoming request using Nimbus JOSE JWT, extracting the user ID, assigned roles, and unique JWT identifier (jti) without database lookups.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: JwtAuthenticationFilter validates HMAC-SHA256 signature using a shared secret; extracts subject, claims `roles`, and claim `jti`; populates ReactiveSecurityContext.

core_mechanisms.name: Sub-5ms Token Revocation Gate via Redis JTI Blacklist Filter
core_mechanisms.description: Queries the distributed Redis cache for key `blacklist:jti:<jti>` to verify that the token has not been revoked prior to its standard expiration (e.g. following explicit user logout or administrative account lock).
core_mechanisms.technical_details: ReactiveRedisTemplate executes `EXISTS blacklist:jti:<jti>` in sub-2ms; returns Mono<Boolean>; if true, terminates request chain with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

core_mechanisms.name: Token-Bucket Distributed Rate Limiting via Redis Lua Scripts
core_mechanisms.description: Protects internal microservices from denial-of-service and brute-force attacks by enforcing a strict rate limit of 100 requests per second per IP/user using Redis token bucket scripts.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Spring Cloud Gateway `RequestRateLimiterGatewayFilterFactory` configured with `RedisRateLimiter(100, 150)`; evaluates tokens remaining atomically via Redis EVALSHA.

core_mechanisms.name: Header Propagation & Identity Sanitization
core_mechanisms.description: Strips any spoofed upstream identity headers and injects trusted cryptographic claims (`X-User-Id`, `X-User-Role`, `X-Forwarded-For`) into downstream request headers for consumption by internal microservices.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Gateway filter mutates ServerHttpRequest: `request.mutate().header('X-User-Id', userId).header('X-User-Role', role).build()`.

core_mechanisms.name: RFC-7807 Problem Details Global Exception Interception
core_mechanisms.description: Catches all perimeter authentication failures, expired tokens, missing headers, and rate-limit violations, converting raw Netty exceptions into RFC-7807 compliant JSON problem details payloads.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: DefaultErrorWebExceptionHandler overridden to serialize ProblemDetails schema with fields `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`, and ISO-8601 `timestamp`.

auth_cache.label: Redis Cache
auth_cache.overview: Provides distributed, in-memory, sub-millisecond key-value storage and concurrency synchronization across the banking microservices. Running Redis 7 Alpine, it serves as the cryptographic token state coordinator for Refresh Token Rotation (RTR), storing token family trees and session hashes to immediately detect token replay attacks. It maintains a high-speed JTI blacklist for logged-out tokens with auto-expiring TTLs matching token lifespans. Additionally, auth_cache enforces distributed idempotency locks (`SET tx:<id> 'PROCESSING' NX EX 60`) on financial mutations to eliminate duplicate button clicks, and caches customer account balance snapshots with a 30-second TTL that are proactively purged upon any balance mutation.

specs.protocol: RESP (REdis Serialization Protocol) v3 over TCP
specs.concurrency_model: Single-threaded event-driven execution kernel utilizing I/O multiplexing (epoll) with atomic Lua script execution
specs.persistence_tier: In-Memory RAM with Append-Only File (AOF) configured to appendfsync everysec and periodic RDB snapshotting
specs.sla_target: Command latency < 1.0ms p99 at 10,000 ops/sec; sub-millisecond lock acquisition

core_mechanisms.name: Refresh Token Family Tracking & Replay Breach Detection Sets
core_mechanisms.description: Maintains cryptographic token family sets (`token_family:<session_id>`) and token metadata hashes. If a previously rotated (revoked) refresh token is submitted, Redis identifies the compromise and enables immediate deletion of the entire token family.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Stores token state in hash `refresh_token:<token_id>` with fields `status: ACTIVE|REVOKED`, `session_id`, `user_id`. Family set `token_family:<session_id>` holds all member token IDs.

core_mechanisms.name: Sub-Millisecond JTI Blacklist with Auto-Expiring TTL
core_mechanisms.description: Stores unique JWT IDs (jti) of revoked access tokens upon logout. Every key is set with an explicit TTL equal to the token's remaining lifetime (max 900 seconds), ensuring zero memory bloat.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Command `SET blacklist:jti:<jti> "revoked" EX <remaining_seconds>` executed on logout; queried via `EXISTS` during gateway perimeter authentication.

core_mechanisms.name: Distributed Idempotency Locking via SET NX EX
core_mechanisms.description: Synchronizes incoming mutating commands across distributed engine nodes. Uses Redis atomic key allocation with NX (Not Exists) and EX (Expiration) flags to guarantee that identical transactions cannot execute concurrently.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Command `SET tx:<idempotency_key> "PROCESSING" NX EX 60`; returns 'OK' if lock acquired, or null/nil if duplicate request is in-flight.

core_mechanisms.name: Balance Read-Through Cache with Event-Driven Invalidation
core_mechanisms.description: Caches customer balance query results under `account:balance:<account_id>` with a 30-second sliding expiration to reduce Oracle database read load. Evicted proactively via `DEL` upon any balance mutation.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Command `SET account:balance:<id> <json> EX 30` on read-through; mutation service issues `DEL account:balance:<source>` and `DEL account:balance:<dest>` upon commit.

core_mechanisms.name: Atomic Rate Limiter Evaluation using Evaluated Lua Scripts
core_mechanisms.description: Executes pre-loaded Lua scripts directly inside the single-threaded Redis kernel to evaluate token-bucket decrements and timestamps atomically without distributed race conditions.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Runs atomic script calculating available tokens: `redis.call('get', tokens_key) - requested`; sets TTL on bucket key.

acc_svc.label: Account Service
acc_svc.overview: Manages the complete lifecycle of customer identities, authentication workflows, Know Your Customer (KYC) regulatory compliance, and account provisioning. Implemented in Spring Boot 3 with Spring Data JPA and connected to the master Oracle XE database, this microservice handles customer onboarding, BCrypt password hashing, session issuance, and the cryptographic mechanics of Refresh Token Rotation. It exposes administrative APIs for compliance officers to inspect government documents and transition KYC statuses (PENDING, VERIFIED, REJECTED). Upon identity verification, it provisions unique 12-digit account numbers across Savings, Checking, and Credit portfolios, initializing zero-balance ledger records in customer_balance_master while orchestrating read-through caching with Redis.

specs.runtime: Spring Boot 3.3.x, OpenJDK 21 LTS, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate 6.5, HikariCP
specs.protocol: HTTP/1.1 REST / JSON downstream of API Gateway; Oracle JDBC over TNS
specs.concurrency_model: Virtual Threads (Project Loom) / multi-threaded worker pool managed by HikariCP (max-pool-size: 20, min-idle: 5)
specs.persistence_tier: Oracle XE 21c tables (users, roles, user_roles, accounts, customer_balance_master); Redis (:6379) for sessions and tokens
specs.sla_target: Authentication endpoint response < 40ms; account provisioning < 80ms; KYC status update < 50ms

core_mechanisms.name: Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) State Machine with Redis Family Storage
core_mechanisms.description: Issues single-use refresh token cookies paired with 15-minute access tokens. Upon refresh, invalidates the used refresh token and rotates to a new cryptographically secure token while maintaining family trees in Redis.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: AuthService validates incoming refresh cookie against `refresh_token:<id>` in Redis; revokes old token and issues Set-Cookie header with `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=604800`.

core_mechanisms.name: Cryptographic Credential Hashing with BCrypt (Work Factor 12)
core_mechanisms.description: Protects customer credentials by hashing passwords using BCrypt with an adaptive work factor of 12 before persisting to the Oracle `users` table, resisting brute-force and dictionary attacks.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: BCryptPasswordEncoder(12) invoked during registration and login credential verification; password plaintext never logged or retained in memory.

core_mechanisms.name: KYC Identity Onboarding & Document Verification Workflow
core_mechanisms.description: Enforces regulatory Know Your Customer compliance by capturing government ID metadata, validating format rules, and gating account capabilities until an administrator transitions kyc_status to VERIFIED.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: User entity maintains `kyc_status` enum (PENDING, VERIFIED, REJECTED); KycService enforces that unverified users cannot initiate fund transfers or receive account provisioning.

core_mechanisms.name: Deterministic 12-Digit Account Provisioning & Balance Master Initialization
core_mechanisms.description: Generates cryptographically random, collision-resistant 12-digit account numbers for verified customers, atomically inserting account metadata and initializing a corresponding 0.0000 PHP balance record.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: @Transactional method creates `accounts` record and inserts matching row into `customer_balance_master` with balance_amount=0.0000, held_balance=0.0000, and version=0.

core_mechanisms.name: Read-Through Cache Orchestration with Automatic Stale-Eviction
core_mechanisms.description: Coordinates balance queries by checking Redis first. On cache miss, reads from Oracle XE and populates Redis with a 30-second TTL, reducing master database load while ensuring fresh data after mutations.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: BalanceInquiryService checks `account:balance:<id>` in Redis; on miss, queries `BalanceMasterRepository.findById()`, serializes to JSON, and stores in Redis with EX 30.

tx_engine.label: Core Mutation Engine
tx_engine.overview: Serves as the central mission-critical transaction and balance processing kernel of the retail banking platform. Operating on Spring Boot 3 with high-performance HikariCP connection pools and Apache Kafka clients, it enforces absolute double-entry bookkeeping guarantees and zero-tolerance balance integrity. The engine processes funds transfers, bills payments, and balance adjustments using the Transactional Outbox Pattern to decouple HTTP request ingestion from distributed Kafka execution. For mutations, it executes database-level pessimistic row locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) on customer_balance_master to serialize concurrent access and prevent double-spending. It automatically routes transactions exceeding 10,000,000.0000 PHP into a Maker-Checker review state with balance holds, enforcing strict segregation of duties (maker_id != checker_id) while maintaining continuous metrics emission to Prometheus.

specs.runtime: Spring Boot 3.3.x, OpenJDK 21 LTS, Spring Data JPA, Spring Kafka 3.2, HikariCP (max-pool-size: 30, min-idle: 5)
specs.protocol: HTTP/1.1 REST / JSON; Oracle JDBC / SQL*Net; Apache Kafka Binary Protocol
specs.concurrency_model: Concurrent thread pool executing isolated database transactions with strict pessimistic row locking and Kafka partition-aligned consumer workers
specs.persistence_tier: Oracle XE 21c (customer_balance_master, transfers, bills_payment, outbox_events); Redis (:6379) for idempotency locks; Kafka (:9092) for event streaming
specs.sla_target: HTTP 202 Ingestion < 15ms; end-to-end Kafka partition settlement < 85ms (p99 < 150ms at 200 TPS)

core_mechanisms.name: Pessimistic Row Locking via SELECT FOR UPDATE
core_mechanisms.description: Acquires exclusive database row-level write locks on balance master rows (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) in deterministic account ID order to serialize concurrent transactions on the same account and mathematically eliminate race conditions and deadlocks.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Repository method annotated with `@Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE)`; generates Oracle `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` SQL; concurrent threads block until transaction commits or rolls back.

core_mechanisms.name: Transactional Outbox Pattern with Guaranteed At-Least-Once Delivery
core_mechanisms.description: Persists the initial transfer entity and a serialized outbox command record into Oracle XE within the exact same atomic local database transaction. A background worker polls outbox rows via `SKIP LOCKED` and streams them to Kafka.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: @Transactional block writes to `transfers` and `outbox_events` (status: 'PENDING'); OutboxPublisherWorker queries with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and produces to Kafka with `acks=all`.

core_mechanisms.name: Maker-Checker Segregation of Duties (> 10M PHP Soft Holds)
core_mechanisms.description: Automatically intercepts high-value transactions (> 10,000,000.0000 PHP), placing a soft hold on source account funds (`held_balance += amount`) and transitioning the transfer to PENDING_APPROVAL. Requires an independent teller to approve.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Evaluates `amount > 10_000_000.0000`; increments `held_balance`; sets status `PENDING_APPROVAL`; approval endpoint strictly enforces `checker_user_id != maker_user_id`.

core_mechanisms.name: Distributed Idempotency Interceptor via Redis Locks
core_mechanisms.description: Intercepts mutation requests bearing an `X-Idempotency-Key` header, validating and acquiring an atomic lock in Redis (`SET tx:<key> 'PROCESSING' NX EX 60`). Duplicate requests within 60 seconds are rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Spring HandlerInterceptor evaluates header; executes Redis `SET NX EX 60`; on failure, returns RFC-7807 Conflict Problem Details.

core_mechanisms.name: Partition-Keyed Kafka Event Streaming (Ordered by source_account_id)
core_mechanisms.description: Publishes transfer commands to Kafka topic `banking.transfers.commands` partitioned by `source_account_id`. Ensures that all transactions affecting a specific account are processed sequentially by a single partition consumer thread.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: KafkaTemplate.send(topic, partitionKey=source_account_id, payload); consumer group `ledger-mutation-workers` maintains strict in-order settlement per account.

core_mechanisms.name: Saga Compensation & Dead Letter Topic (DLT) Fault Isolation
core_mechanisms.description: Handles transient failures and irrecoverable poison pills. Transient database lock timeouts trigger exponential backoff retries on `banking.transfers.retry`; unrecoverable errors route to `banking.transfers.dlt` with compensating reversals.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Spring Kafka `DefaultErrorHandler` configured with `ExponentialBackOff(1000L, 2.0)` and `DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer` directing to `.dlt` after 3 failed attempts.

master_db.label: Master Ledger DB
master_db.overview: Serves as the authoritative System of Record (SoR) for all transactional state, relational account mappings, customer balances, and pending outbox events. Deployed on Oracle Database Express Edition 21c, it provides ACID transaction guarantees with Read Committed isolation and row-level locking capabilities. The database schema enforces mathematical and business invariants via native database-level CHECK constraints (`balance_amount >= held_balance` and `balance_amount >= 0`), making balance corruption or overdrafts physically impossible at the storage layer. It hosts the operational outbox table (outbox_events) which guarantees zero message loss between local database commits and distributed Kafka publishing.

specs.runtime: Oracle Database Express Edition 21c (21.3.0) on Oracle Linux
specs.protocol: Oracle TNS (Transparent Network Substrate) / SQL*Net v2 over TCP
specs.concurrency_model: Multi-Process Architecture with Dedicated Server Processes, Row-Level Locking (TX Locks), and System Change Number (SCN) MVCC
specs.persistence_tier: Oracle Datafiles (.dbf) with redo log groups, undo tablespaces for rollback segment management, and System Global Area (SGA) buffer cache
specs.sla_target: Single-row indexed query < 2ms; SELECT FOR UPDATE lock acquisition < 5ms; transaction commit < 10ms

core_mechanisms.name: Exclusive TX Row-Level Locks via SELECT FOR UPDATE
core_mechanisms.description: Acquires row-level exclusive locks in data blocks without page or table escalation. Prevents any other transaction from modifying locked balance records while allowing concurrent uncommitted reads via Undo segments.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Oracle marks the lock byte in the data block header (Interested Transaction List - ITL); concurrent sessions enqueue on row lock (TX mode 6) until COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

core_mechanisms.name: Storage-Enforced Invariant CHECK Constraints (Overdraft Prevention)
core_mechanisms.description: Protects against ledger bugs by enforcing constraints directly in the database kernel: `chk_positive_balance` (`balance_amount >= 0`), `chk_positive_held` (`held_balance >= 0`), and `chk_available_balance` (`balance_amount >= held_balance`).
core_mechanisms.technical_details: DDL: `CONSTRAINT chk_available_balance CHECK (balance_amount >= held_balance)`. If an UPDATE violates this, Oracle raises `ORA-02290: check constraint violated`.

core_mechanisms.name: Transactional Outbox Event Staging with SKIP LOCKED Polling
core_mechanisms.description: Stores outbox event rows within the application transaction. Worker threads query unread events with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, allowing multiple worker threads to dequeue events simultaneously without contention.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: SQL: `SELECT * FROM outbox_events WHERE status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY created_at FETCH FIRST 50 ROWS ONLY FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.

core_mechanisms.name: Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) via Undo Segments
core_mechanisms.description: Ensures that readers never block writers and writers never block readers. Balance inquiries read before-image snapshots reconstructed from Undo segments, guaranteeing consistent views without locking rows.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Oracle evaluates System Change Number (SCN); reads data block, substituting undo blocks for any rows modified by active uncommitted transactions.

core_mechanisms.name: ACID Atomic Transfers via Two-Row Balance Mutation Blocks
core_mechanisms.description: Executes debit and credit operations within a single atomic database transaction. If either operation fails or violates a constraint, Oracle rolls back all changes via transaction undo logs.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Ensures total system conservation: SUM(balance_amount) before = SUM(balance_amount) after across internal account transfers.

audit_db.label: Audit Trail DB
audit_db.overview: Houses the immutable, legally admissible compliance audit vault and historical transaction journal for all ledger mutations. Running on PostgreSQL 15+ Alpine, it is decoupled from the master operational database to guarantee that audit logging never impacts real-time transfer latency. The primary table, ledger_mutation_audit, is protected by native database triggers that raise immediate compliance exceptions on any attempted UPDATE or DELETE SQL commands, rendering the audit log strictly append-only. It ingests mutation events asynchronously from Kafka topic banking.transfers.events via an isolated consumer group, indexing records by account_id, transaction_id, and audit_timestamp to support rapid regulatory discovery and audit reporting.

specs.protocol: PostgreSQL Wire Protocol v3 over TCP
specs.concurrency_model: Process-based worker architecture with Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) and non-blocking asynchronous streaming ingestion
specs.persistence_tier: PostgreSQL Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) with durability (fsync=on), dedicated heap files, and composite B-tree indexes
specs.sla_target: Insert throughput > 1,500 records/sec; auditor account chronological query < 8ms for 1,000,000 rows

core_mechanisms.name: Strict Append-Only Enforcement via Native PL/pgSQL Triggers
core_mechanisms.description: Prevents any modification or deletion of historical audit logs. A BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger raises a PL/pgSQL exception on any attempted data tampering, even by administrative database users.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Trigger `trg_no_update_delete_mutation_audit` executes `prevent_audit_modification()`: `RAISE EXCEPTION 'Compliance Violation: ledger_mutation_audit is strictly append-only. UPDATE and DELETE operations are forbidden.'`.

core_mechanisms.name: Asynchronous Event Projection from Kafka Commit Log
core_mechanisms.description: Decouples audit logging from the transaction execution path. An independent consumer group (`audit-vault-workers`) streams `TransferExecuted` events from Kafka and writes audit entries without slowing down master transactions.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Kafka listener consumes from topic `banking.transfers.events`; executes batch insert into `ledger_mutation_audit`; commits offset to Kafka only after PostgreSQL commit.

core_mechanisms.name: Cryptographic Correlation & Idempotency Key Auditing
core_mechanisms.description: Records the complete lineage of each financial mutation, storing the correlation `transaction_id`, `idempotency_key`, `client_ip`, and `operator_id` alongside the before and after balance amounts.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Stores NUMERIC(18,4) before_balance and after_balance, mutation_type ('DEBIT', 'CREDIT', 'HOLD_PLACED'), and TIMESTAMPTZ audit_timestamp.

core_mechanisms.name: Composite B-Tree Chronological Indexing for Fast Auditor Queries
core_mechanisms.description: Optimizes regulatory queries and customer history lookups using composite indexes on `(account_id, audit_timestamp DESC)` and `transaction_id`, returning account timelines in sub-10ms.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Indexes: `CREATE INDEX idx_audit_account ON ledger_mutation_audit(account_id, audit_timestamp DESC)` and `CREATE INDEX idx_audit_tx_id ON ledger_mutation_audit(transaction_id)`.

core_mechanisms.name: Air-Gapped Operational Decoupling (Fault Isolation from Master DB)
core_mechanisms.description: Ensures that database maintenance, vacuuming, or high read query loads on PostgreSQL never block balance mutations in Oracle XE, providing complete fault isolation between operational and audit tiers.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Separate database container and storage volume; failure of audit_db causes Kafka consumer lag to accumulate safely without disrupting core balance operations.

apis_and_contracts.contract_details: Append-only table storing audit_id, transaction_id, account_id, mutation_type, mutation_amount, before_balance, after_balance, operator_id, and audit_timestamp.
PostgreSQL compliance trigger prohibiting UPDATE and DELETE commands on ledger_mutation_audit.

broker.label: Kafka Event Bus
broker.overview: Serves as the high-throughput, fault-tolerant event backbone and distributed commit log for the banking architecture. Running Apache Kafka 3.7+ in modern KRaft (Kafka Raft Metadata) mode without ZooKeeper dependencies, the broker guarantees strict chronological event ordering within account partitions by hashing source_account_id as the partition key. It decouples synchronous ingestion from balance mutation, audit logging, and customer alerts through distinct consumer groups. The broker enforces at-least-once message delivery, idempotent producer configurations, dead-letter routing for poison pills, and is bundled with a web-based management UI on port 8085 for real-time visualization of partition offsets, consumer group lag, and broker metrics.

specs.protocol: Kafka Binary Protocol over TCP (PLAINTEXT / SASL_PLAINTEXT)
specs.concurrency_model: Partition-level parallelism; multi-threaded network processors and I/O threads handling segment append and zero-copy page cache reads
specs.persistence_tier: Append-only segmented commit logs on disk with configurable retention policies and OS page cache optimization
specs.sla_target: Producer publish latency < 5ms (acks=all); consumer delivery latency < 10ms; zero message loss with replication factor

core_mechanisms.name: Partition Key Hashing for Strict Per-Account Sequence Preservation
core_mechanisms.description: Routes transfer commands to specific partitions by computing a MurmurHash2 on `source_account_id`. Guarantees that all mutations affecting an account are processed in exact chronological sequence by a single consumer thread.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Kafka partition assignor maps `hash(source_account_id) % num_partitions`; eliminates concurrency race conditions between sequential transfers on the same account.

core_mechanisms.name: KRaft Metadata Consensus (ZooKeeper-Less Quorum Controller)
core_mechanisms.description: Manages broker cluster metadata, topic configurations, and partition leader elections using an internal Raft consensus protocol, eliminating external ZooKeeper latency and failover delays.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Operates with `--override process.roles=broker,controller`; metadata stored in `@metadata` internal partition log.

core_mechanisms.name: Competing Independent Consumer Groups with Offset Commit Isolation
core_mechanisms.description: Allows multiple downstream systems to consume identical event streams at their own pace without interference. Consumer groups `ledger-mutation-workers`, `audit-vault-workers`, and `notification-workers` maintain independent committed offsets.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Broker tracks offsets per group in `__consumer_offsets` topic; consumer lag in notifications never stalls audit logging or ledger settlement.

core_mechanisms.name: Idempotent Producer Delivery & Exactly-Once Semantics (EOS)
core_mechanisms.description: Configures producers with `enable.idempotence=true` and `acks=all`. The broker tracks Producer ID (PID) and sequence numbers to reject duplicate message publishes caused by network retries.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Producer config: `acks=all`, `retries=Integer.MAX_VALUE`, `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=5`; broker deduplicates duplicate network packets automatically.

core_mechanisms.name: Dead Letter Topic (DLT) & Delayed Retry Exponential Backoff
core_mechanisms.description: Provides dedicated topics for failed messages: `banking.transfers.retry` for transient failures with backoff delays, and `banking.transfers.dlt` for poison pills, ensuring clean separation of healthy and faulted records.
core_mechanisms.technical_details: Headers inject metadata: `x-original-topic`, `x-exception-message`, `x-exception-stacktrace`; monitored by Kafka UI on port 8085.

notif_svc.label: Notification Service
notif_svc.overview: Operates as an asynchronous event-driven worker microservice dedicated to real-time customer communications, regulatory transaction receipts, and teller alert dispatching. Built on Spring Boot 3 with Spring Kafka, it joins the notification-workers consumer group, subscribing to banking.transfers.events without blocking the core mutation engine. When a transaction completes or enters review, it formats comprehensive debit/credit receipts including pre/post balances, timestamps, and reference codes. It dispatches push notifications and rich HTML email receipts to customer inboxes, and pushes urgent alert events to branch teller consoles when high-value transfers (> 10M PHP) require Maker-Checker compliance sign-off.

telemetry.label: Observability Stack
telemetry.overview: Provides real-time end-to-end performance monitoring, SLA compliance tracking, distributed metrics scraping, and visualization for the entire banking platform. Combining Prometheus v2.45 and Grafana v10, this stack scrapes Micrometer Actuator metrics (/actuator/prometheus) across all Spring Boot microservices every 5 seconds. It measures live Transactions Per Second (TPS) against the project's 200 TPS benchmark, tracks p50, p95, and p99 latency percentiles against the 150ms SLA target, monitors HikariCP connection pool saturation (active vs idle connections), and tracks Kafka consumer lag across all topics. Pre-configured Grafana dashboards display live operational health, alerting operators to database lock contention, memory leaks, or message pileups in real time.

specs.persistence_tier: Prometheus Time Series Database (TSDB) with on-disk chunk storage (15-day retention); Grafana SQLite internal database for dashboard provisioning
specs.sla_target: Scrape duration < 200ms per endpoint; PromQL query execution < 50ms; Dashboard refresh interval 5s
